questions.q: A one-time legacy-system conversion with 40,000 supplier records at go-live is best suited to which method?
options: Manual entry, one supplier at a time
FBDI
A phone call to Oracle support
Printing the records and re-typing them later
questions.explain: Large one-time volumes are exactly what FBDI's template-and-import pipeline is built for.

questions.q: Where do you go to upload an FBDI ZIP file into UCM?
options: The File Import and Export page under Tools in the navigator
A direct FTP connection to the database server
The Create Journal page
A third-party cloud storage link
questions.explain: File Import and Export, found under Tools in the Fusion navigator, is the page used to upload a file into a UCM account.

questions.q: What are the three building blocks every FBDI load uses?
options: A password, a username, and a browser
A template, an interface table, and an import process
A printer, a scanner, and a fax machine
A REST API, a webhook, and a token
questions.explain: Every FBDI load follows the same pattern: a template maps to an interface table, and an import process moves validated rows from there into application tables.

questions.q: Why should you never insert, delete, or reorder columns on an FBDI template's data tab?
options: Because Excel will crash if you do
Because the column headers are literal interface-table column names, and rearranging them breaks the mapping between spreadsheet and database columns
Because Oracle charges a fee for each column changed
There is no actual risk in doing this
questions.explain: A template's columns map one-to-one onto an interface table's columns. Changing their order or set breaks that direct mapping.

questions.q: Why is Supplier Import commonly one of the first FBDI loads run in a new Oracle Fusion implementation?
options: Because almost nothing else in Payables or Procurement can happen until suppliers exist in the system
Because suppliers are the least important data in the system
Because supplier data never needs validation
Because it is the only FBDI template Oracle provides
questions.explain: Payables invoices, purchase orders, and procurement activity all depend on supplier records already existing, which is why loading suppliers typically comes first.

questions.q: Why does FBDI require data as CSV rather than uploading the Excel workbook directly?
options: Because Excel files are always too small
Because CSV files look nicer when opened
Because Oracle cannot read any Microsoft file formats
Because interface tables only care about raw column values, and CSV strips away formatting, formulas, and other structure the import doesn't need
questions.explain: CSV reduces a workbook to its essential data — rows and comma-separated values — which is exactly what an interface table load process needs and nothing more.

questions.q: What is the most important thing to remember about 'success' reported by Load Interface File for Import?
options: It is identical to the data being fully imported into the application
It means the file was permanently deleted from UCM
It only means the data is staged in an interface table, which is why confusing it with final success is a common mistake
It guarantees zero rows will ever be rejected later
questions.explain: This lesson stresses that staging success and final import success are two separate claims — mistaking one for the other is a common source of confusion.

questions.q: What has to happen BEFORE the product-specific import process can do its job?
options: Nothing — it can run on an empty interface table with no issue
Rows must already be staged in the relevant interface table, typically via Load Interface File for Import
The Oracle Fusion environment must be restarted
All existing live records must first be deleted
questions.explain: The product-specific import process reads rows that are already staged in an interface table — which is the outcome of the previous Load Interface File for Import step.

questions.q: Why would a consultant query an interface table directly instead of only relying on the import process's report?
options: Because reports are never produced by Oracle Fusion
Because querying is required before every single screen click in Oracle Fusion
Because a direct query shows the raw, current state of the staged data with no summarizing or interpretation
Because interface tables cannot be queried at all
questions.explain: Interface tables are ordinary database tables. A direct query gives you the unfiltered, current state of what's staged, which a summarized report doesn't always fully capture.

questions.q: Why are bank statement imports typically run on a recurring cadence rather than as a one-time conversion?
options: Because Oracle requires it to be run exactly once per year
Because bank statements never contain useful data
Because ongoing cash reconciliation depends on statements being loaded regularly, unlike a one-time supplier or journal conversion
Because a one-time load is technically impossible for this module
questions.explain: Unlike a one-time go-live conversion, bank statement loading supports ongoing operational reconciliation, so it needs to happen on a predictable, recurring schedule.

questions.q: Which process actually validates staged payables invoice rows and creates real, live invoices?
options: Load Interface File for Import
Import Payables Invoices
Import Journals
Generate CSV File
questions.explain: Import Payables Invoices is the product-specific import process for this module — it validates staged rows and creates real invoice records.

questions.q: Which interface table does AutoInvoice read staged transaction lines from?
options: GL_INTERFACE
AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE
RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL
FA_MASS_ADDITIONS
questions.explain: RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL is the Receivables transaction-line staging table that AutoInvoice reads from.

questions.q: In the scenario, Load Interface File for Import succeeds cleanly before Import Payables Invoices rejects 13 of 200 rows. What does this tell the consultant?
options: The ZIP file itself must be corrupted
The entire batch must be rebuilt from scratch
The rejections are business-rule issues at the row level, not a file-structure problem, since the file already passed load-time validation
Nothing can be concluded from this information
questions.explain: Because load-time validation already succeeded, the consultant can rule out file-structure problems and focus on business-rule validation at the row level.

questions.q: What does the 'purge only successfully processed records' option remove?
options: Every row in the interface table regardless of status
Nothing — this option does not exist
Only rows that were never attempted
Only rows that already became real application records, since there's no further reason to keep their staged copy
questions.explain: This narrower, lower-risk option clears rows that have already successfully become real records, since their staged copy no longer serves a purpose.

questions.q: What is the correct, repeatable workflow for fixing rejected rows described in this lesson?
options: Delete the entire interface table and start the whole conversion over from scratch
Ignore the rejections and move on to the next module
Identify exactly which rows were rejected and why, correct only those specific values, and resubmit only that corrected set
Re-run the original full file every time, regardless of how many rows failed
questions.explain: The correct approach isolates and corrects only the specific rows that failed, then resubmits just that scoped set — avoiding reprocessing already-successful data.

questions.q: Why does Create Invoice in Spreadsheet have both header fields and line fields, just like the FBDI Payables Invoice Import template?
options: Pure coincidence with no underlying reason
Because an invoice itself has two levels — header and line — and that business shape doesn't change based on which tool is used to load it
Because ADFdi requires exactly two sections in every spreadsheet
Because line fields are optional and rarely used
questions.explain: The header/line structure reflects the actual shape of an invoice as a business object, not a quirk of either specific loading tool.

questions.q: Why is Receivables transaction loading described as 'almost always FBDI'?
options: Because Receivables has no ADFdi option available at all, under any circumstance
Because Receivables transactions are always exactly five rows
Because FBDI is required by law for all receivables transactions
Because receivables transaction volume typically originates from another system (billing, point-of-sale, subscription platforms) rather than from a person typing directly into Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Unlike journals or invoices where ad-hoc, interactive entry is common, receivables data overwhelmingly originates externally, making FBDI the dominant method.

questions.q: What does ADF Desktop Integration (ADFdi) actually do?
options: It zips CSV files and uploads them to UCM
It extends Oracle's application framework into Microsoft Excel, letting a live Fusion page talk directly to a connected spreadsheet
It is a reporting tool unrelated to data entry
It replaces the need for Oracle Fusion entirely
questions.explain: ADFdi connects Excel directly to a live Fusion page, letting users download, edit, and upload data with the same validation the web page applies.
